newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine government decries U.S trade sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Argentine government decries U.S trade sanctions.

text.p: The Argentine government on Thursday said U.S. trade sanctions imposed on the country in a patent dispute were unfair and illegal.
"It is a totally unjust sanction which has no bearing on reality," President Carlos Menem told local television.
"But it does not damage in the least the excellent relations between the United States and the Republic of Argentina," the president, a staunch U.S. ally, quickly added.

On Wednesday, the United States said it would withdraw half of Argentina's duty-free trade benefits because patent laws passed in 1995 and 1996 continued to allow Argentine laboratories to copy drugs developed by U.S. companies.
The Radical Party, the main opposition force, called the U.S. move irksome and groundless.

"It is not only surprising but also obviously aggravating to the Argentine Congress and people that their parliamentarian job be evaluated and disqualified by a foreign government which, using as its only tool its dominant position in the concert of nations, resorts to sanctions in violation of international treaties," it said in a statement.
A trade group representing major Argentine drug lababoratories urged Menem to take the case to the World Trade Organization.
